content:
maria: Heads-up — AcmeCorp is asking for a Dedicated commitment for Q4 seasonal spikes. They want a proposal by EOD tomorrow. They gave rough traffic expectations but no formal numbers yet.

sam: can we get their expected qps / concurrency? that determines gpu type and pods.

alex: from sales: Acme expects 3x baseline traffic in November and December, peak windows 8 hours/day. They want 99.9% p95 latency SLAs. Budget: flexible but wants justification for reserved hours vs burst.

jordan: rough calc. If baseline is 60 concurrent requests at 1.2k tokens per request avg, peak concurrency ~180. With our H100 runtime and avg tokens/sec per GPU ~2500 (gen load), we need ~0.072 GPUs per concurrent stream so ~13 GPUs for peak. add buffer for batching inefficiency -> +20% = 16 GPUs.

lee: region note: eu-west-1 has limited H100 inventory in Dedicated fleet for Nov-Dec. If Acme prefers eu only we may need to reserve now or propose A100 fallback which affects latency/cost.

maria: we should propose two skus: H100-reserved and A100-fallback with automatic routing. include cost delta and expected p95 impact.

alex: customer asked about buffer policy — they want ability to burst 2x for short windows. our current Dedicated buffer policy is 20% reserved + best-effort burst into shared pool. if they need contractual burst we need to size commit and price it.

jordan: proposal draft numbers: 
```
Option A (H100, contractual): 16 H100 GPUs reserved, 8% monthly overprovision buffer for short bursts, guaranteed 24/7. Estimated GPU-hours/month = 16 * 24 * 30 = 11,520.
Option B (H100 + burst): 13 H100 GPUs reserved (peak baseline), 20% cost buffer in price, allow best-effort burst up to 2x during 8h peaks, no guaranteed burst SLA. Est hours = 9,360 reserved + meter burst.
Option C (A100 fallback): 20 A100 GPUs reserved in eu-west, lower per-GPU throughput, expect 10-15% higher latency and 18% higher token cost.
```

sam: we should sanity-check with recent telemetry. jordan, can you pull last 3 months of Acme's token/sec and p95 latency on hosted? want to validate model assumptions.

jordan: on it. quick note on pricing math: H100 reserved list price X vs A100 Y — nina can you run the P&L for committed hours at both prices (include network/egress and monitoring cost)?

nina: will run. also flag: committed reserved months reduce our spot capacity for other customers. need finance sign-off for larger long-term commitment discounts.

lee: ops constraint: if we lock 16 H100 in eu-west for them and then another large customer asks for Q4, we may be capacity-constrained. suggest offering cross-region routing: primary eu-west, fallback us-west with data residency caveats. include replication/latency implications.

alex: customer prefers EU but open to multi-region for failover if we guarantee data never leaves EU for primary processing. they asked about cost for geo-redundant vs single-region.

maria: action items:
- jordan: finish telemetry + refined GPU count by EOD (1742008900).
- nina: pricing scenarios for Options A/B/C and P&L impact by EOD.
- lee: check H100 inventory projection for eu-west Nov-Dec and confirm ability to reserve 16 GPUs; if not, provide timeline for procurement.
- alex: communicate preliminary options to Acme, clarify burst contractual needs.

ops-bot: Reminder: capacity request submitted (REQ-4271). Current approval queue: infra-capacity > finance.

sam: one more operational note — our buffer policy doc says we can do 10% guaranteed buffer + 20% best-effort. if customer is asking 2x burst guaranteed that's a different product tier. mention that in proposal.

jordan: updated numbers after quick telemetry check (rough, subject to verification): avg token/sec during peak week = 220k tokens/sec across their app, concurrency distribution matches earlier calcs. with our batching profile that maps to ~15 H100 for 99th percentile. recommending Option B with contractual ramp and an add-on for guaranteed burst windows (charge per reserved extra GPUs during N peak days).

maria: good. let's keep proposal lean: show cost/latency tradeoffs, regional constraints, and an explicit buffer/burst carve-out. alex will present to customer.

alex: I'll send the draft to Acme's procurement this afternoon and flag the guaranteed burst as a separate line item. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
